input: This review considers whether the quality laboratory should make an additional hire. The laboratory has 16 full-time staff, and last year overtime ran at 6% of paid hours. A substantial amount of overtime might appear to point towards a need for more staff. However, the workload that produced it is concentrated in two seasonal peaks, and this distribution changes the picture. Replacing half the overtime with one additional hire would cost $80k per year fully loaded, and the hire would be paid for the full year, whereas the peaks occupy only part of that year. The trade-off can be stated in one sentence: $80k committed for twelve months against cover that is needed in two peaks. Even if half the overtime were replaced, overtime would still stand at 3% of paid hours, and the remaining peak load would still fall on the existing staff in the peak weeks themselves. Overtime, by contrast, is bought only in the weeks the peaks occur and stops when they pass, so its cost tracks the demand that causes it. The record behind this assessment is one year of paid hours; a single year does not show whether the peaks are lengthening, and the decision should be reopened if they do. The case for the hire would need demand outside the peaks, which last year's record does not show. On balance, the recommendation is not to add a hire: laboratory management, which holds the decision, should keep the overtime arrangement for the coming year and review the position if overtime outside the peaks begins to grow.
